$comment: Every name reachable from a published entry point, tagged with its maturity (§5.5 of PRD.md). `npm run check:maturity` fails if a published name is missing here, if a name here is no longer published, if a tag is outside the four states, or if a non-stable name has no note. Nothing defaults: an untagged export is a build failure, which is the point of the file. Withdrawals are recorded in `removed` rather than deleted: a name that left the surface keeps the tag it held, the release that dropped it and the section of CHANGELOG.md that announced it, and the check fails if such a name is somehow published again, if its announcement does not name it, or if it was removed in anything but a major version.
policy: stable — documented, relied on by the shell or by the published docs as the way to do the thing, and present at the 0.9.0 close. A breaking change needs a major version.
experimental — shipped and typed, shape still being learned from use. May change in a minor, with a changelog line.
internal — not reachable from a published entry point, so it never appears in this file; the state is named because the policy needs all four.
deprecated — superseded and still working. Removed only in a major, after one minor of warning here and in the changelog.
derived: The baseline is mechanical: a name reachable from a published entry point at aed9fd6 (the 0.9.0 close) is stable; anything newer is experimental, because 0.10 and 0.11 are both still unpublished and a shape cannot be learned from use that has had none. Four older names were moved by hand and say why in `notes`: the signing helpers, whose shape the `0.8` measurements settled but had not yet shipped. The core freehand ink group is no longer in either list — FR-18 withdrew it, and its fifteen names are in `removed`.

notes.BoxPoint: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.CanvasBudget: New in the unreleased 0.12 as §6.1’s combination rule made callable: the effective ceiling, which of the four candidates set it, and what each asked for. Experimental because the shape is new and `applied` may grow a fifth candidate.
notes.CanvasCeilingSource: The four §6.1 ceiling names, as a union rather than an enum, because the set is the specification’s and a new member means the specification changed.
notes.CanvasProbeOptions: The seams of `probeCanvasCeiling` — the limit, the ladder, and the canvas factory a test can hand it. Exported because the factory is the only way to test a ceiling that no CI environment can allocate.
notes.DEFAULT_MAX_PATTERN_UNITS: New in the unreleased 0.12 as the default half of FR-27’s pattern bound. The value is fixed by the requirement, so changing it is a specification amendment rather than a minor-version API break; the export is tagged experimental only because no release has carried it yet.
notes.DestinationKind: New in the unreleased 0.12: the display mode a `/Dest` names, which decides which of its numbers is a vertical position. The set is the PDF specification’s, so a new member means the specification changed — `Unknown` exists so a writer that invented one still resolves to a page.
notes.ExternalPageText: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.ExternalTextIndex: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.FindPlanError: New in the unreleased 0.12: the kind behind `patternKind`, so a host can tell an over-long pattern from an uncompilable one without reading `patternError`. Adding a third reason later is additive; changing what the two existing ones mean is not.
notes.MIN_RENDER_SCALE: New in the unreleased 0.12: §6.1’s minimum render scale, which the renderer lowers toward and then stops at. The value is fixed by the requirement, so changing it is a specification amendment, not a minor-version API break.

notes.MergePlan: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.

notes.MergeSource: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.PDF_ERROR_CODES: The published list behind the union, new in the unreleased 0.12. A code is never reused and never removed in a minor; a new one may be added, which grows this array and is not a breaking change.
notes.PadSize: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.PagePlan: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.

notes.PdfArrangeResult: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.PdfBytes: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.PdfDestinationPosition: New in the unreleased 0.12 as the second half of a destination: the place, alongside the page. Its fields are the specification’s own three values, and a `null` in each is a defined answer (“keep what the reader has”) rather than a gap, which is the part a host is most likely to misread.
notes.PdfDownloadOutcome: New in the unreleased 0.12 as what `download()` resolves to — the name, whether the file carries the edits, and the refusal when it does not. The promise used to resolve to nothing, which is why the silent fallback could be a fact only the hook knew. `null` (no download happened) is part of the shape, so a host that awaits has to handle the cancelled case rather than assume a file was written.
notes.PdfEngineRequirement: New in the unreleased 0.12, from the #249 finding: the way a feature says that one of its own behaviours needs an engine newer than the package floor, and what the reader gets below that release. Experimental because no release has carried it and the prose half (`below`) is the part a host may want restructured into a message it renders itself.
notes.PdfError: Unpublished: 0.12 introduces it and no release has carried it yet, so its shape has had no use to learn from. The code list inside it is a different promise — §3.6 forbids reusing a code for a new meaning, and that holds whatever this tag says.
notes.PdfErrorCode: Unpublished, and the union is §3.6’s seventeen names exactly. Extending it is additive; renaming or dropping one would break the contract the row exists to keep, which is why the list is asserted against PRD.md rather than trusted — and why #242 was willing to pay that cost rather than advertise a name nothing produces: `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE` left the union with it, because its only claimed producer was a table row for an exception class no shipped engine stamps.
notes.PdfFlattenResult: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.PdfPageArrangement: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.PdfSaveRefusal: New in the unreleased 0.12: the reason a save could not carry the reader’s edits. One member today, `xfa`, because that is the one document shape whose packet the writer cannot rebuild. A third reason is an addition; renaming what `xfa` means would be a specification change, not a version bump.

notes.STRUCTURE_LINK_OWNERSHIP_MINIMUM: The release 6.2.108 lacks, measured off the engine rather than looked up in a changelog: `enableLinkOwnership` is absent from 6.2.108’s `build/pdf.mjs` and present in 6.3.289’s. Experimental as a *name* — the number is a fact about the engine, and `src/features/structure.engine-floor.test.tsx` refuses the browser matrix if the two ever disagree.
notes.StructureFeatureState: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.UsePdfMergeOptions: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.UsePdfMergeResult: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.VirtualSlotPage: New in the unreleased 0.12: the per-page box that lets a host place a page without making it a child of its row, which is what FR-08 needs a layout switch to survive. `VirtualSlot` itself is unchanged and stays stable; this is the field added to it, so the shape is one the shell has already rendered and a host may ignore.
notes.buildTextIndex: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.describeMergeSources: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.ensureCanvasCeiling: New in the unreleased 0.12: the realm-cached probe behind §6.1’s “detection, not labels”. The shell calls it after the first paint; a host calls it to move that measurement earlier, before the viewer mounts.
notes.findSignatureFields: see signFields — the same open decision about where the signing surface lives.
notes.invalidatePageText: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.isCancellationCode: New in the unreleased 0.12, and the function that keeps FR-04 checkable: the three cancellation codes are not failures, and a host needs one call rather than a list of its own to tell them apart.
notes.isPdfError: New in the unreleased 0.12. It tests §3.6’s shape (a code from the list, beside a message) rather than `instanceof` or the class name, and that choice is load-bearing for cancellations — so it is tagged experimental because no release has had a consumer, not because the rule is uncertain.
notes.isSignable: see signFields — the same open decision about where the signing surface lives.
notes.mergeDocuments: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.orderFeatures: New in the unreleased 0.12 as §3.7’s registration contract: it validates a feature list (duplicate id, missing dependency, dependency cycle — each a `CONFIGURATION_ERROR`) and returns it with every dependency before its dependents. The shell calls it itself, so a host only needs it to build something the shell does not: their own toolbar, or their own `mergeFeaturePageProps` call. Experimental because no release has carried it yet.
notes.outwardPageOrder: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.parseDestinationPosition: New in the unreleased 0.12: the per-kind reading of `[page, /Mode, …]`. Exported because a host that resolves destinations of its own — a search-over-bookmarks box, a generated TOC — needs the same table, and the whole point of FR-01’s one-heuristic rule is that there is not a second copy.
notes.probedCanvasCeiling: The cached answer on its own, for a host that wants to read the ceiling without being the one that triggers the probe.
notes.resolveCanvasBudget: New in the unreleased 0.12 as §6.1’s minimum of four ceilings. Exported because the shell is not the only caller that needs the rule: a host computing its own render options, or reading back why a page is soft, needs the same arithmetic rather than a second copy of it.
notes.resolveDestination: New in the unreleased 0.12: the page *and* the place, from one walk of the reference. `resolveDestinationPageIndex` stays as it was and is what most callers want, so this is an addition rather than a change of shape.
notes.signFields: writing a drawn mark into a `/Sig` appearance stream crossed the per-feature size gate, and where signing lives is an open decision. The *capability* is not in question; the entry point it is reached from is.
notes.signatureContent: see signFields — the same open decision about where the signing surface lives.
notes.structureFeature: published first in 0.10.0 or 0.11.0: the shape is typed and shipped, and this release is the use it is being learned from.
notes.structureLinkOwnershipAvailable: Unpublished: it joins the surface in the 0.12 that #249 wrote, and it is the readable form of the same fact. Likely to fold into a general “does this engine have it” helper rather than stay a structure-only export, which is what experimental is for.
